text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: Canary p99 latency spike detected for model rw-serve-v2 on the hosted API. Alert fired at 1763501234. Metrics: p95 -> 1.1s (baseline 220ms), p99 -> 7.4s (baseline 480ms). Streaming stalls observed on chunked responses.
Alex M: seeing it too, spikes coincide with the canary rollout that started ~1763501100.
Priya R: @Alex M are we still routing 5% to canary?
Alex M: yes 5% split via routing policy canary-v2.
Dan S: paging oncall now. grabbing logs and traces.
incident-bot: PagerDuty triggered for on-call: Priya R.
Priya R: I'm on it. quick check: dashboard shows increased queue length on gw-proxy and higher CPU on the canary pool g4dn-small.
Katelyn L: can we confirm model change? Which model binary was pushed to canary?
Alex M: pushed 'rw-serve-v2' with a new attention-kernel patch and quant profile q8. Diff was small but the runtime scheduling changed.
Miguel T: trace link: https://redwood.internal/traces/1763501200?span=canary-run (posted for team)
Priya R: quick triage: p50 stable, p95 up x5, p99 tail huge. streaming stalls after ~8s where chunks stop arriving. logs show repeated KV cache misses + retries.
CS Lead: customer impact — CS ticket ID: #3981. One paid customer reported partial streaming outputs. Could be timeouts. Need expected ETA for mitigation.
Priya R: immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0% (rollback split), 2) scale canary pool, 3) rollback canary to previous model. Which order?
Dan S: prefer reduce to 0% first to stop new hits, then decide.
Alex M: agree. I'll flip traffic if someone confirms.
Katelyn L: also worth checking if new kernel introduced blocking path for streaming flush.
Priya R: executing traffic cut.
Priya R: command run:
```
# switch routing policy to remove canary
redwoodctl rollout set-traffic --policy canary-v2 --percent 0 --confirm
```

incident-bot: Routing update started by Priya R.
Alex M: seeing drop in canary requests in metrics within 30s. p95 trending down but p99 still elevated from in-flight requests.
Miguel T: streaming stalls count decreased after routing change but some in-flight streams are still stalled.
CS Lead: notifying impacted customer: msg sent to #cs-alerts with instructions and temporary workaround (retry / shorter chunk window).
Priya R: next step: decide whether to rollback model binary or roll forward with patch. Thoughts?
Katelyn L: logs show an unexpected synchronization on the attention kernel when kv-cache miss triggers a fallback path. My bet is the kernel change. Rollback to previous model binary and quant profile.
Alex M: +1 rollback. I'll trigger a canary rollback now.
Priya R: rollback command:
```
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service rw-serve --to-revision r2026-04-18-9 --target canary
```

incident-bot: Deploy rollback started by Alex M. CI/CD shows canary rollback completed at 1763501700.
Dan S: verifying metrics and traces now. p95 back to ~240ms, p99 down to ~520ms. Streaming stalls nearly gone.
Miguel T: sampling traces show earlier stalls matched kernel call sequence A -> B -> C where B took >6s under q8. After rollback traces are normal.
Priya R: running post-mortem checklist: collecting logs, saving trace snippets, capturing the diff of the kernel patch, and ticketing the root cause.
CS Lead: I've updated the customer with the rollback outcome and ETA for a follow-up postmortem. They appreciate the quick rollback.
Katelyn L: open action items: 1) gate canary kernel changes behind perf test for streaming stalls, 2) add alert for streaming chunk stall rate, 3) add automatic rollback policy if p99 > 1s for >2m on canary.
Alex M: created ticket INF-2148 for gating perf tests + INF-2149 for automatic rollback policy.
Priya R: handing off to oncall-night: @Dan S will monitor for the next 4 hours and follow up in the morning.
Dan S: oncall ack, I'll watch the dashboards and validate there are no residual regressions.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity: Sev3. Start 1763501234, mitigated 1763501700. Postmortem owner: Katelyn L.
Priya R: thanks team. quick thumbs: :thumbsup: if you have nothing else.
Alex M: :thumbsup:
Dan S: :thumbsup:
Katelyn L: :thumbsup:
CS Lead: leaving note in #cs-ops with timeline and customer message.
Miguel T: saving traces and logs under /incidents/1763501234/ for postmortem.
Priya R: closing thread here, will follow up with a short postmortem doc and link to the perf regression repro steps.
